question.leadin: Give the following about the Adams family.
question.text: John Adams was married to this early feminist, who advised him to "remember the ladies" in one of their numerous correspondences.
question.clue: This person wrote another letter asking to "remember the ladies and be more generous and favorable to them than your ancestors."

swap.leadin: Name these pieces of legislation aimed at the British colonies.
swap.text: This collection of punitive measures, also known as the Coercive Acts, included the Quartering Act, and forbade un-approved gatherings of more than five people.
swap.clue: Following the passage of these laws, Thomas Hutchinson was replaced byThomas Gage as one colony's governor.

question.text: Attucks was the first person killed in this event on March 5, 1770. Paul Revere made an engraving showing this event, in which five colonists died in Massachusetts' capital.
question.clue: The engraving The Fruits of Arbitrary Power by Henry Pelham depicts this event by showing a linear arrangement of eight men standing outside a custom house.

swap.leadin: Give the following about America's most famous pamphleteer, Thomas Paine.
swap.text: This 1776 work by Paine argues that no mother should treat her children as horribly as Britain had treated the American colonies; therefore, the colonies should declare independence.
swap.clue: Another chapter of this work claims that a certain monarch did little but "make war and give away places".

question.text: This British general surrendered to American forces at the Battle of Yorktown. He later served as the military governor of Ireland.
question.clue: His namesake "Code" is credited with preventing bureaucratic corruption throughout British rule in India, and he later resigned as viceroy of Ireland in protest over Parliament's denial of Catholic rights.

swap.text: This American general and "Fighting Quaker" opposed Cornwallis through much of the Southern campaign, culminating in the Battle of Guilford Court House.
swap.clue: He appointed John Cox and Charles Pettit as assistants in a role in which he replaced Thomas Mifflin, that of Quartermaster General.

question.text: This general of the Continental Army led a miscalculated assault against the British during the battle, the failure of which led to him being court-martialed.
question.clue: This man wrote numerous letters to Congress during the New York campaign, seeking to replace his superior, George Washington.

swap.text: Cornwallis's surrender to the Americans at Yorktown basically marked the end of this war, which started at the battles of Lexington and Concord.
swap.clue: In the leadup to this war, the term "virtual representation" described tariffs passed by Charles Townshend.

question.leadin: This general may have gained his nickname for leading a charge at the Battle of Green Springs.
question.text: Name this American general who was humiliated at the Battle of Paoli. This general negotiated the Treaty of Greenville after defeating Blue Jacket in the Battle of Fallen Timbers.
question.clue: Following that victory against Blue Jacket, this man negotiated the Treaty of Greenville.

swap.leadin: In 1938, over 100 people dressed as this man marched in protest of FDR's plan to reform the presidency.
swap.text: Name this man whose best-known feat was accomplished in conjunction with William Dawes, helping Samuel Adams and John Hancock avoid capture.
swap.clue: This man, who notably depicted the Boston Massacre, was later joined by William Dawes and Samuel Prescott in one mission.

question.leadin: Name some legislative bodies of pre-United States America.
question.text: This 1765 meeting in New York City decried the lack of jury trials and claimed a right to self-taxation in its Declaration of Rights and Grievances, and saw Timothy Ruggles serve as its president.
question.answerHtml: the Stamp Act Congress [prompt on partial answers]
question.clue: This act which required that legal documents, newspapers, and other paper goods have a certain mark affixed to them, providing revenue for the British Crown.

swap.text: The tea-dumpers were drawn from this secret organization, led in part by Samuel Adams. They were responsible for the tarring and feathering of many a British tax collector.
swap.answerHtml: the Sons of Liberty [accept Sons of Violence or Sons of Iniquity from any turncoats out there]
swap.clue: The Loyal Nine, a predecessor to this organization, hung Andrew Oliver in effigy and raided Lieutenant Governor Thomas Hutchinson's house while protesting a certain piece of legislation.

question.leadin: "Remember the ladies" by answering the following about women from early American history.
question.text: A woman from this family, Mercy Warren, advocated for a Bill of Rights in her Observations on the New Constitution. Her brother from this family, James, coined the phrase "taxation without representation is tyranny."
question.clue: A woman from this family married James Warren and was the first woman to write a history of the American Revolution.

swap.text: In Melville's Israel Potter, Potter tries to rescue this man from prison. This man led an operation that allowed for Henry Knox's noble train of artillery while he was leading a group who eventually replaced him with Seth Warner.
swap.clue: This man was held prisoner by the British after unsuccessfully attempting to take Montreal under General Philip Schuyler.

question.leadin: This battle was fought immediately after the victory over drunken Hessians at Trenton.
question.text: Name this New Jersey battle, a Revolutionary War victory that saw American troops spill across Quaker Bridge.
question.clue: At a critical point in this engagement, John Cadwalader arrived with militiamen to support the fleeing forces of Hugh Mercer, who the British mistook for George Washington.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the role pine trees played in the colonial US.
swap.text: Joseph Reed, who designed the Pine Tree Flag in 1775, represented Philadelphia as part of committees of correspondence created by this politician. James Otis and this politician co-authored the Massachusetts Circular Letter.
swap.clue: Thomas Gage exempted John Hancock and this person when Gage offered to pardon people who laid down their arms during the Battles of Lexington and Concord.

question.leadin: While working for the Culper Ring, Elizabeth Burgin helped save hundreds of people from these places because women were the only people able to visit them.
question.text: Name these places that the British hulked near New York City. A Martyrs' Monument in Fort Greene Park honors more than 11,000 Americans who died in these places during the Revolutionary War.
question.answerHtml: prison ships [prompt on prisons by asking “in what structures?”; prompt on ships by asking “serving what purpose?”]

swap.leadin: This incident was inscribed into historical memory with a poem in Spenserian stanzas by Thomas Campbell, who perpetuated the myth that Joseph Brant was responsible.
swap.text: Name this 1778 incident in a namesake valley in Pennsylvania, where Loyalists and Indian soldiers under John Butler massacred women and children gathered at Forty Fort.
swap.clue: During the Revolutionary War, the Iroquois joined with the Loyalist group known as Butler's Rangers and murdered 340 Patriots in this event. It was followed by the similar Cherry Valley massacre in New York.

question.leadin: Answer the following about pre-Revolutionary War protests of British duties, FTPE.
question.text: Opposed in the "Letters of a Westchester Farmer" by Samuel Seabury, this organization was created in 1774 by the Continental Congress to ensure the enforcement of non-importation of dutied goods. It was based on a similarly named program started in Virginia in response to the Townshend Acts.
question.clue: Sherman was one of the signatories of this 1774 agreement, which called for a boycott of all British goods.

swap.leadin: As of September 2017, Mark Meckler's COS group has secured support from 12 state legislatures for one of these events centered on a balanced budget amendment.
swap.text: Identify these events that can happen with approval from two-thirds of state legislatures according to Article V of the Constitution. There hasn't been one of these events since 1787.
swap.clue: One of the oldest attendees was the oddly named Daniel of St. Thomas Jenifer, while another attendee, James Wilson, developed an infamous proposal.
